figures.teaches: Each stone type forms from a specific urine abnormality and pH, so prevention targets that abnormality.
figures.content: Five rows, each with a small crystal icon: 'Calcium oxalate' (low volume, high calcium, high oxalate, low citrate, high uric acid; prevention: water, normal dietary calcium with less sodium, thiazide/citrate/allopurinol only when the 24-hour urine shows the matching abnormality); 'Calcium phosphate' (high urine pH, hypercalciuria, distal RTA; treat cause); 'Uric acid' (persistently low urine pH; water, alkalinization); 'Struvite' (urease-producing infection, alkaline urine; complete removal, treat infection); 'Cystine' (inherited cystinuria; very high fluid, alkalinization, specialist). Side panel 'Water works': 'Borghi 1996, 199 first calcium stone formers: recurrence 12% vs 27% at 5 years'. Footer: 'Target urine volume >=2.5 L/day (AUA 2026)'.

figures.teaches: Obstruction is suspected, confirmed and drained in sequence, with urgent drainage for infection and hourly monitoring after relief.
figures.content: Six vertical steps: 'Suspect' (anuria, palpable bladder, prostate symptoms, pelvic cancer, stones, catheter; partial obstruction can have normal urine output) -> 'Check the bladder' (scan or palpate; flush or change a blocked catheter) -> 'Image' (ultrasound for hydronephrosis, may be absent early or when dehydrated; CT for stones) -> red step 'Drain' (urethral or suprapubic catheter for outlet; stent or nephrostomy for ureter; urgent tonight if fever or sepsis, EAU 2026 strong; delay stone removal until sepsis resolves) -> 'Watch the urine' (hourly output, BP, sodium, potassium, magnesium, creatinine; replacement as the attending directs) -> 'Find the cause'. Side box: 'qSOFA >=2: RR >=22, altered mentation, SBP <=100'.
